assets.modifications: Simplified the generated concept into original SVG paths using the public docs navy, cyan and white palette. The published docs copy adds a 160 px intrinsic width and height so Markdown renderers such as GitHub show it at mark size; the game copy keeps the bare 512 viewBox for Godot import. Website icons rendered from the published SVG on 2026-10-16 with rsvg-convert (librsvg) and ImageMagick, no other edits: wolf-override-mark-96.png (96x96, transparent) for browsers without SVG favicons, and apple-touch-icon.png (180x180, the mark at 148 px centred on the opaque #101e2c landing surface colour, since iOS fills transparency with black).
assets.implementation_status: Provisional mark used by the game title, README, public landing page and website favicons (SVG, 96 px PNG and 180 px Apple touch icon).

assets.source_or_tool: Made by code on 2026-10-18 (a Python build script kept outside the repository with the logo set's notes) from the approved wolf mark (entry wolf-override-logo-mark, apps/docs/public/wolf-override-mark.svg, paths reused unchanged) and the name WOLF OVERRIDE set in Montserrat weight 800, shaped with HarfBuzz and converted to outlined SVG paths, so the files need no font.

assets.modifications: Horizontal layout: the mark left, the name right under a cyan rule, 25 units of clear space on every side (1620x320 viewBox). for-dark-bg: white name, #8BE3FF rule and ring (4,843 B, SHA-256 cce2dfd41bea23e162501084eddb3747cb5682ea0a048a9e74cfb8cbaae72036). for-light-bg: navy #091533 name, #00ACED rule and ring so they show on light grounds (4,843 B, SHA-256 6fa18c574823be1ad9985e6151f8ca5060f906c97e639efbc872fda480fe8512). Not used by the game, whose title keeps the mark and live text. assets.modifications: Sixteen generated clips. Startup, 22.05 kHz: boom (0.5 s), small boom (0.3 s), clank (40 ms), thud (80 ms), hum loop (1.0 s), klaxon (three 120 ms square chirps, 0.5 s), servo loop (1.2 kHz sine with a 6 Hz vibrato, 1.0 s), winch loop (90 Hz saw with a 7 Hz wobble, 1.0 s), whine (sine sweep 300 Hz to 1.8 kHz, 0.6 s) and, added 2026-10-13 in an AI-assisted pass (Claude Code) and not yet picked by ear, chirp (two soft sine blips a fifth apart, 1.32 kHz then 1.98 kHz, 0.15 s) and actuator (a low-passed saw gliding 150 to 230 Hz and back with a 38 Hz gear ripple, 0.24 s), and fuse_tick (a 1 ms strike on 2.35 and 3.9 kHz partials over a 520 Hz body, 70 ms; added later on 2026-10-13 in the same kind of pass, not yet picked by ear); all three are pure tones that draw nothing from the seeded noise, so the earlier clips keep their bytes. Detailed, 44.1 kHz (added 2026-10-10): relay_spark (recipe A: snap, 120 Hz pulsing buzz and crackle, 0.34 s), records_arc (recipe B: N-wave crack, short housing knock, restrike, pulsing tail with the late crackle faded out, 0.65 s), bolt_arc (recipe B: 0.5 s build of buzz and crackle, then the crack and restrike, 0.8 s) and growl_warning (recipe C: chaotic subharmonic throat in a metal chassis with a wandering swell and two snarl bursts, 1.2 s). Retired 2026-10-10: the generated hiss loop, arc crackle and growl (replaced by the recordings and the detailed recipes). Played through AudioStreamPlayer nodes on the Effects bus; volume and pitch are set per use.
